Inverse document frequency of skills over postings

Source: R/reference_professions.R
skill_idf.Rd

Computes \(idf_s = \log(N / n_s)\), where \(N\) is the number of postings with at least one skill and \(n_s\) the number of those postings that mention skill \(s\): the same document-frequency scheme as compute_idf_classification(), returned as a named vector so that profiles of two classifications can share one weighting.

Usage

skill_idf(
  skills,
  id_col = "general_id",
  skill_col = "idescoskill_level_3",
  ids = NULL
)

Arguments

skills

A data.frame with one row per posting and skill (duplicates are ignored), with columns id_col and skill_col.

id_col

Name of the posting id column. Default "general_id".

skill_col

Name of the skill column. Default "idescoskill_level_3".

ids

Optional vector of posting ids: when supplied, only these postings enter \(N\) and \(n_s\).

Value

A named numeric vector, one element per skill, named by the skill and sorted by name. Attribute n_postings holds \(N\).

Examples

skills <- data.table::data.table(
  general_id = c(1, 1, 2, 3),
  idescoskill_level_3 = c("a", "b", "a", "c")
)
skill_idf(skills)
#>         a         b         c 
#> 0.4054651 1.0986123 1.0986123 
#> attr(,"n_postings")
#> [1] 3
